# SEV-1 INCIDENT - RELEASE BLOCKER
**Title:** Statements are filing some payments under the wrong kind of transaction, or dropping the payee name
**Owner:** Payments Operations
**Disposition:** Do not ship this release until it is resolved

## What customers reported

Over the past few days support has collected a run of tickets that all share one
shape: the money itself moved fine, but the app files the payment under a category
that does not match what the customer actually did, or shows the wrong name - or
no name at all - beside it. In every case the row that misbehaves carries one very
particular, uncommon form of raw statement text; everyday rows are labeled exactly
as before. The tickets below are anonymized, but the raw narration each customer
pasted is reproduced verbatim, because that raw text is what makes each case
reproducible.

> "I wrote a cheque against my account and the app just lists it as a general
> transfer now - nothing marks it as a cheque anymore. My earlier cheques were
> tagged correctly. The only thing sitting in that row's note is the cheque's own
> number, nothing else around it."

> "My salary came in and the amount is right, but where my employer's name should
> be the app now just prints the word `NACH`. The raw text on that row looks like
> `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` - it used to lift the employer's name off the end
> of that reference, and now it is picking up the wrong piece of it."

> "On some transfers that come in, the sender's name is blank now. Those rows all
> share the same reference layout - a short block of letters, then a long string
> of digits, then the name - for example `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR`. The name
> sitting at the end just is not being pulled through anymore; the name column
> comes out empty."

The same batch of complaints also covers two quieter cases that are about the
category rather than the name. The token confirmation charge a bank posts when a
new auto-debit mandate is set up - a small nominal amount, with the note flagging
it as a mandate - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being
recognized as a verification entry. And a refund that came back on a card is
landing as a plain refund for some customers when it should read as a card
reversal; a customer on a different type of account sees the same kind of refund
labeled correctly, so the wrong label appears to depend on the account category.

## Scope of impact

Everyday activity - normal purchases, routine transfers, regular deposits - is
categorized and named correctly, which is precisely why this slipped through QA and
why our monitoring dashboards looked healthy. The breakage is confined to a small
set of unusual transaction forms - among them a note or reference that is exactly
a certain number of digits wide - each one hinging on some exact shape of the raw
row rather than anything about the customer, and each form individually uncommon. But they occur right across the customer base, so they
generate a steady trickle of "why is this labeled wrong" tickets and, more
damaging, they poison the spending-category summaries and payee histories that
several downstream features rely on. That combination is why we are treating it
as ship-blocking rather than a backlog item.

## What we need from engineering

The labeling path is fully deterministic and runs offline - hand it the same
transaction and it reproduces the same wrong answer every time - so each of these
is reproducible on demand and can be pinned down exactly. Get the affected forms
labeling and naming correctly again, and do it without disturbing any transaction
that is already labeled right today. A fix that rescues these cases but nudges the
behavior of ordinary, currently-correct transactions is not acceptable: the pass
condition is simply that the specific problem payments described above come out
right and everything else stays exactly where it is.
I'll start by exploring the codebase to understand the transaction labeling path.

# Report: Transaction Labeling / Payee-Extraction Code in `/app`

## 1. Repository at a glance

The repo is a single Flask micro-service ("transaction-enrichment-python") that receives raw bank statement transactions as JSON and enriches them with category, subcategory, merchant type and counterparty (`partyName`). Everything is pandas + `np.select` rule tables driven by large regex constant banks. There is **no ML/NER**, and **no test suite**.

```
/app
├── .gitignore
├── Dockerfile                                   # python:3.9.2, gunicorn, port 9898
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                                 # deps: Flask 1.1.2, pandas 1.2.4, fuzzywuzzy,
    │                                            #       python-Levenshtein, scipy, sklearn, matplotlib
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py                          # Flask app factory + logging + request timing
        ├── Controller.py                        # HTTP routes + per-bank pipeline dispatch (936 lines)
        ├── UtilityScripts/                      # cross-bank stages + regex constant banks + enums
        └── BankScripts/                         # 35 per-bank labeling scripts
```

Total ≈ 11,200 lines of Python across 54 files.

---

## 2. Absolute file paths

### 2.1 Core / cross-bank pipeline (`UtilityScripts`)

| Path | Lines | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py` | 936 | Flask routes `/`, `/categorizeTransaction`, `/recurrentTransactions`; giant `if bank == ...` dispatcher that runs the pipeline stages in fixed order |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/__init__.py` | 31 | Flask app, logger, `import categorizationapp.Controller` |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py` | 66 | **The extraction primitives**: `clean_input_df`, `sep_by_*` splitters, `py_extract` (regex extract), `fuzzy_match` |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/TransactionCategoryEnums.py` | 171 | `TransactionCategory` enum (level-1 label) — CHEQUE_*, TRANSFER, REFUND, CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL, ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION, AUTO_MANDATE_CHARGES, NACH, ECS, … |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py` | 136 | `TransactionSubcategory` enum (level-2 label) — SALARY, LOAN_REPAYMENT, ECS_BOUNCE, REFUND, INTERNAL_PAYMENT, … |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py` | 191 | ~190 giant merchant/purpose regex constants shared across banks (SALARY, LOAN_REP, CREDIT_CARD, INSURANCE, NBFC, HFC, PMT_GTW, TDS, TECHNICAL_BOUNCE, …) |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` | 432 | **Bank-specific narration parsing regexes**, incl. all named `*_PATTERN*` capture groups used for payee extraction (SBI/HDFC/PNB/Kotak/Union/UCO/SCB/City Union…), plus `ACC_VERIF`, `BANK_VER*`, cheque/NEFT/IMPS/FT/OS/MB patterns, bank-name stripping lists |

| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CleanName.py` | **1971** | **Largest file — canonicalises `partyName`** (merchant name normalisation), also fixes `merchantType`/`transactionSubcategory` |

### 2.2 Per-bank labeling + payee extraction scripts (`BankScripts`, 35 files)

All under `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/`:

`Andhra.py` (103), `AuSmallFinanceBank.py` (102), `Axis.py` (188), `BOB.py` (167), `BOI.py` (89), `Bandhan.py` (78), `BankOfMaharashtra.py` (235), `Canara.py` (201), `Central.py` (93), `Citi.py` (151), `CityUnion.py` (162), `DCB.py` (107), `Federal.py` (112), `HDFC.py` (276), `ICICI.py` (245), `IDBI.py` (247), `IDFC.py` (107), `Indian.py` (78), `Indusind.py` (263), `Karnataka.py` (101), `KarurVyasa.py` (130), `Kotak.py` (327), `PNB.py` (192), `Paytm.py` (107), `RBL.py` (147), `SBI.py` (193), `SVC.py` (68), `Saraswat.py` (81), `SouthIndian.py` (98), `StandardCharted.py` (208), `Syndicate.py` (141), `TamilnadMerchantile.py` (89), `UCO.py` (107), `UnionBank.py` (152), `YES.py` (142)

Each exposes exactly one entry point `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType[, accountHolder])`.

### 2.3 Tests

**None exist.** No `test_*`, `*_test.py`, `conftest.py`, `pytest.ini`, `tox.ini`, CI config, or fixture data anywhere in the repo (verified by glob for `*{test,Test,spec,conftest,pytest,fixture}*` → no matches, and by the full file listing). The only "testing" artefacts are commented-out dendrogram/matplotlib blocks inside `SalaryDetection.py` (lines 27–32) and `RecurrentTxns.py` (lines 16–21).

---

## 3. Structure of the labeling pipeline

### 3.1 Request → response flow (`Controller.categorizeTransaction`, lines 69–936)

```
POST /categorizeTransaction
  payload: { bank, acc_type, accountUID, accountHolder, isPFMEnabled, transactions[] }
  1. pd.json_normalize(payload['transactions'])              -> DataFrame
  2. AppUtil.clean_input_df()                                 # strip description, numeric amount/balance
  3. dispatch on `bank` (35 branches, string keys listed below)
       categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType[, accountHolder])
  4. if accountType == "CREDIT_CARD":  card_clean_names() -> card_purpose()
  5. purpose(transactions, accountType)                       # subcategory + merchantType
  6. clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)             # canonical partyName
  7. if accountHolder: internal_payment(...)                  # fuzzy self-transfer detection
  8. if accountType == "SAVING": salary_detection(...)        # clustering-based salary
  9. if isPFMEnabled: pfm_categorization() -> simple_description()
 10. transactions.to_json(orient='records')
```

Bank keys accepted: `ANDHRA_BANK, SBI, ICICI, HDFC, IDFC, BANK_OF_INDIA, IDBI, KARNATAKA, UNION_BANK, BANK_OF_BARODA, PNB, SYNDICATE, KOTAK, CANARA, AXIS, INDUSIND, KARUR_VYASA, BANK_OF_MAHARASHTRA, CITY_UNION, UCO, YES, FEDERAL, RBL, CENTRAL_BANK, DCB, CITI, PAYTM_BANK, STANDARD_CHARTERED, AU_SMALL_FINANCE_BANK, BANDHAN, INDIAN_BANK, SOUTH_INDIAN, SARASWAT_BANK, SVC_BANK, TAMILNAD_MERCANTILE`. Unknown bank → `{"error": "<bank> Bank Not Found."}`. The 24-line block is copy-pasted verbatim per bank.

### 3.2 Inside a bank script — the canonical 4-block shape

Every `BankScripts/*.py` follows the same idiom (best seen in `IDBI.py`, `HDFC.py`, `Kotak.py`):

```python
conditions_choices = [ [<boolean Series>, <label or Series>], ... ]     # ordered, first match wins
df = pd.DataFrame(data=conditions_choices, columns=['conditions','choices'])
transactions['<col>'] = np.select(df['conditions'], df['choices'], default=<fallback>)
```

Block order:

1. **`transactionCategory`** — narration regex + `type` (DEBIT/CREDIT) + `amount` thresholds + occasionally `shift(1)` row-adjacency (to detect bounce/reversal pairs, e.g. `HDFC.py:98-99`, `StandardCharted.py:60`). Fallback is `"TRANSFER"`.
2. **`transactionSubcategory` / `merchantType`** — bank-local overrides, seeded to `""`.
3. **`partyName`** — the payee/counterparty extraction table (see §4). Post-processed with `.str.title().str.strip()` and junk-stripping regexes.
4. **cleanup passes** — additional `np.select` rounds that blank out garbage `partyName` (`^Na$`, digits-only, single letter), plus (IDBI, HDFC) a `city` column derived from POS narrations.

`transactions['party2']` = `partyName` with spaces removed — a space-insensitive shadow column that `Purpose.py` / `CleanName.py` match against in parallel with `partyName`.

### 3.3 Columns produced

`transactionCategory`, `transactionSubcategory`, `merchantType`, `partyName`, `party2`, `internalName`, `isInternalPayment`, `city` (IDBI/HDFC), `Group_ID`, `pfmCategoryOne`, `pfmCategoryTwo`, `pfmCategoryType`, `pfmSimpleDescription`.

Input columns consumed: `description` (raw narration), `remark` (cheque no. / UTR), `amount`, `type`, `balanceAfterTransaction`, `transactionDate`.

---

## 4. Payee / counterparty extraction — the mechanics

### 4.1 Primitives (`AppUtil.py`)

```python
sep_by_(desc, n1, n2)        # desc.str.split('/').str[n1:n2].str.join('')
sep_by_dash / _wave (~) / _star (*) / _comma / _colon / _under (_) / _brckt ( / _right_brckt )
                             #  ... same delimiter-index slicing family (lines 14-45)
py_extract(desc, pat, index) # desc.str.extract(pat, flags=re.IGNORECASE).get(index), NaN->""  (lines 61-66)
fuzzy_match(s1, s2, dist)    # fuzzywuzzy fuzz.ratio > dist  (lines 48-51)
```

So payee extraction = *(a)* positional token slicing on the narration's delimiter, or *(b)* a named capture-group regex from `BankRegexConstants.py`.

### 4.2 The `ACH-BD-NACH-<PAYEE>` family (NACH / ECS auto-debit mandates)

| Bank file | Line(s) | Pattern → extraction |
|---|---|---|
| `IDBI.py` | 81–88 | `\bETPC.*ACH-BD-` → `sep_by_dash(...,2,3)`; `\bETPC.*ACH-` → dash 1:2; **`^ACH-BD-NACH` → `sep_by_dash(desc,2,3)`**; `^ACH-BD-` → dash 2:3; `^ACH-BARB-` → dash 2:3; `^ACH-` → dash 1:2; `^NACH,` → `sep_by_wave(1,2)`; `^NACH` → `sep_by_(1,2)` |
| `HDFC.py` | 169–174 | **`^ACH D- BD-NACH-` → `sep_by_dash(desc,3,4)`** then `\d`-strip + `.str.strip()`; `^ACH D- BD-` → dash 2:3 + digit strip; `ACH D- TP ACH` → `py_extract(pat="TP ACH (.*)-")`; `^ACH D-\s?(?!(BD-))|^RP|^TP-|^ECS D` → dash 1:2 with `CAMS|TP ACH ` removal; `^SI ` → `SI_PATTERN = ".*[0-9] (.*)-"` |
| `Kotak.py` | 124–138 | `^NACH-SAL-CR-SAL-` → dash 4:5; `^NACH-[A-Z0-9]+-CR-` → dash 3:4; `NACH-RPN-DR-TP ACH` → `py_extract("TP ACH(.*)-")`; `NACH-LEG-DR-BDECS-` → dash 4:5; `NACH-10-DR-BD-|NACH-10-DR-BARB-` → dash 4:5; `^NACH-10-DR-|NACH-LEG-DR-` → dash 3:4; generic AUTO_PAYMENT: dash 1:2, or dash 2:3 when token 1 == `BD` (lines 136–137) |
| `PNB.py` | 142–143, 159 | `^NACH/` CREDIT → `sep_by_(3,4)`; `^ACH/|NACH-DR/|^ECS|NACH- DR/` → `sep_by_(1,2)`; `PNB_AUTO_1 = "CPH/TP ACH (.*)/"` |
| `Axis.py` | 133 | `^NACH-DR- TP ACH` → `py_extract("^NACH-DR- TP ACH (.*)")` |
| `UnionBank.py` | 78–79 | `^NACH/[0-9]` → `sep_by_(2,3)`; `^NACH/` → `sep_by_(1,2)` |
| `BOI.py` | 67–68 | `NACH DR INW - ` / `NACH CR INW - ` → `py_extract("NACH [CD]R INW - (.*) [0-9]+")` |
| `BOB.py` | 106–110 | `^NACH DR INW` → `py_extract("-(.+) [0-9]")`; `/NACHRTN$` → `sep_by_(1,2)` |
| `StandardCharted.py` | 119–122 | `NACH DR IW:` → `sep_by_colon(2,3)` or `(1,2)`; `NACH DR OW` → colon 1:2; `NACH (.*) [A-z]{4}[0-9]{14}` → `py_extract("[0-9]{16} (.*) [A-z]{4}[0-9]{14}")` |
| `KarurVyasa.py` | 93–95 | `ECS TP ACH (.*) NACH`, `ECS (.*)-NACH`, `ECS (.*)- NACH` |
| `IDFC.py` | 76, 80 | `NACH/` → `sep_by_(1,2)`; `NACH~` → `sep_by_wave(1,2)` |
| `ICICI.py` | 137–138 | `NACH_AD_RTN_CHRG~AD|~INGENOT` → `sep_by_wave(4,5)`; else wave 1:2 |
| `Karnataka.py` | 58 | AUTO_PAYMENT + `-NACH-` → `sep_by_(sep_by_dash(desc,3,4), 0, 1)` (nested) |
| `SouthIndian.py` | 63–64 | `^NACH/SIBL` → `sep_by_(2,3)`; ` NACH/SIBL` → last `/` token |
| `Citi.py` | 114 | `NACH:Paid to` → `sep_by_colon(1,2)` |

| `Kotak.py` (constants) | `BankRegexConstants.py:178-179` | `ECS_END = "AD\s?$|BG\s?$|...|IY\s?$"`, `ECS_START = "^TP\s?(ACH)?\s?"` — trims NACH utility-code prefixes/suffixes off the extracted party name |

So `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` → IDBI line 83 (`^ACH-BD-NACH` → dash token 2) or HDFC line 169 (`^ACH D- BD-NACH-` → dash token 3).

### 4.4 Name post-cleaning / canonicalisation

* Per-bank: junk regex strips e.g. `HDFC.py:223` (`"\\,?\\.$|/$|\\*$|\\,{1,2}$|^\\.{2}|\\s?-$|.rzp"`), `HDFC_CLEAN1` (BankRegexConstants:106) blanks `google pay`, `remitter`, `Unregistered`, `xxx`, single letters, etc.
* Bank-name strippers: `CHQ_CLEAN_KOTAK` (line 318), `REMOVE_BANK_CB` (417, Central), `REMOVE_BANK_CITI` (424), `CHQ_CLEAN_SCB` (432), `CHQ_CLEAN`/`CHQ_CLEAN2` (361–362, BOM), `NEFT_DEBIT_STOP`/`NEFT_PAYMENT_STOP` (333–334, Indusind), `LOCATION_CLEAN`/`TRF_STOP_WORDS` (64–65, SBI).
* Cross-bank: `CleanName.clean_names()` (`CleanName.py`, 1971 lines) — one enormous ordered `conditions_choices` list (~1930 rows) mapping alias regexes on `partyName` / `party2` / `description` to canonical merchant names, organised by commented sections: internet, electricity, gas/utilities, entertainment, soft_app, general exp, food, insurance, lender (lines 457–943, the largest block), shopping, online marketplace, education, streaming, medical, crypto, investment, creditcard, mobile recharge, travel, govt service, infra, commute, fuel, IT/web services, HR/freelance, fin_ser, exam, courier/logistics, packaging, donation, bank, neobank, electronics, payment gateway, paytm, google, "fixes" (case/abbreviation normalisation: ICICI/HDFC/RBL/SBI/LLP/Pvt Ltd/Corporation/Restaurant/Supermarket…), private-limited & corporation normalisation, then a final `merchantType` pass and `transactionSubcategory` pass.
* Credit-card twin: `CardCleanNames.card_clean_names()` (927 lines) — same structure but only matches `description`.

## 5. Category / label enums

        [transactions.description.str.contains("^OPENING BALANCE", na=False, case=False) , "OPENING_BALANCE"],
        [transactions.description.str.contains("CASH\\s?BACK|[Cc]ashback|/Rewarde", na=False, case=False) & transactions.type.eq("CREDIT") , "CASHBACK"],

        [transactions.description.str.contains("UPI.*DECLINE|UPI/RET/|UPI.*reversa", na=False, case=False) , "UPI_REVERSAL"],

import re, glob
for f in sorted(glob.glob('BankScripts/*.py')):
    lines = open(f).read().split('\n')
    prev=None
    for i,l in enumerate(lines,1):
        s=l.strip()
        if not (s.startswith('[') and s.rstrip(',').endswith(']')):
            prev=None; continue
        depth=0; pos=None
        for j,ch in enumerate(s):
            if ch in '([': depth+=1
            elif ch in ')]': depth-=1
            elif ch==',' and depth==1: pos=j
        if pos is None: prev=None; continue
        cond=s[1:pos].strip(); choice=s[pos+1:].rstrip(',').rstrip(']').strip()
        if prev and prev[1]==choice and prev[0]!=cond:
            print(f"{f}:{prev[2]}&{i}  choice={choice[:60]}")
            print(f"    A: {prev[0][:160]}")
            print(f"    B: {cond[:160]}")
        prev=(cond,choice,i)
EOF

    if fn: mods[name]=fn[0]
widths=[5,6,7]
for name, fn in mods.items():
    rows=[]
    for w in widths:
        num='1'*w

        rows.append({'description':num,'remark':'','type':'CREDIT','amount':7000})
    try: out=run(fn,rows)
    except Exception as e: print(name,"ERR",e); continue
    cats=list(out.transactionCategory)
    line=" ".join(f"{widths[i//2]}{'D' if i%2==0 else 'C'}:{cats[i]}" for i in range(len(cats)))
    if set(cats)!={"TRANSFER"}: print(f"{name:22s} {line}")
EOF

cd /app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp && python3 - <<'EOF'
import re, glob
sepmap = {'sep_by_':'/','sep_by_dash':'-','sep_by_wave':'~','sep_by_star':'*','sep_by_comma':',','sep_by_colon':':','sep_by_under':'_'}
cond_re = re.compile(r'description\.str\.contains\(\s*"([^"]+)"')
sep_re  = re.compile(r'(sep_by_(?:dash|wave|star|comma|colon|under)?)\(\s*transactions\.description\s*,\s*(\d+)\s*,\s*(\d+)\s*\)')
for f in sorted(glob.glob('BankScripts/*.py')):
    for i,line in enumerate(open(f).read().split('\n'),1):
        s=line.strip()
        if not s.startswith('['): continue
        c = cond_re.search(s); m = sep_re.search(s)
        if not (c and m): continue
        pat = c.group(1); fn = m.group(1); n1=int(m.group(2)); n2=int(m.group(3))
        d = sepmap.get(fn)
        if d is None or n2 != n1+1: continue
        if not pat.startswith('^'): continue
        # only literal-ish prefixes (no regex metachars except ^ and \\b and spaces)
        body = pat[1:]
        if re.search(r'[\[\]().*+?{}|\\$]', body): continue
        if d not in body: continue
        toks = body.split(d)
        # number of complete delimiter-separated tokens consumed
        expected = len(toks)-1 if toks[-1]=='' else len(toks)-1
        # if prefix ends with delimiter, payee starts at index len(toks)-1
        # if not, the last partial token is part of token index len(toks)-1 -> payee is that token or later
        endswith = body.endswith(d)
        exp = len(toks)-1
        note = "ends-with-delim" if endswith else "partial-last-token(payee likely index %d)"%(exp+1 if toks[-1] else exp)
        if endswith:
            if n1 != exp: print(f"{f}:{i} pat={pat!r} {fn}({n1},{n2}) expected {exp}")
        else:
            if n1 == exp:
                print(f"{f}:{i} SUSPECT pat={pat!r} {fn}({n1},{n2}) -> extracts the same token the pattern matched; expected {exp+1}?")
EOF

import sys, re, itertools, importlib.util
import pandas as pd
sys.path.insert(0,'/app/categorizationapp')
from harness import run

def load(path, name):
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
    m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
    return [v for k,v in vars(m).items() if k.startswith('categorize_')][0]

# build corpus of descriptions from every string literal used in description.str.contains in BOTH files
def corpus_from(path):
    src=open(path).read()
    out=set()
    for lit in re.findall(r'(?:description|partyName|party2)\.str\.contains\(\s*"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"', src):
        for alt in lit.split('|'):
            s = alt
            s = s.replace('\\\\b','').replace('\\b','').replace('\\s?',' ').replace('\\s*','').replace('\\.','.')
            s = re.sub(r'\[([A-Za-z])[A-Za-z]*\]', r'\1', s)
            s = re.sub(r'\[0-9\]\{(\d+)(,\d*)?\}', lambda m:'1'*int(m.group(1)), s)
            s = re.sub(r'\[A-Za-z0-9\-\]\{(\d+)(,\d*)?\}', lambda m:'A'*int(m.group(1)), s)
            s = re.sub(r'\[A-Z\]\{(\d+)(,\d*)?\}', lambda m:'A'*int(m.group(1)), s)
            s = re.sub(r'\[A-z0-9\]\{(\d+)(,\d*)?\}', lambda m:'A'*int(m.group(1)), s)
            s = s.replace('[0-9]','7').replace('[A-Z]','K').replace('[A-z]','K').replace('X{7,}','XXXXXXX').replace('X{10,}','XXXXXXXXXX').replace('X{4,}','XXXX')
            s = re.sub(r'\{\d+(,\d*)?\}','',s)
            s = s.replace('.*',' ALPHA BETA ').replace('.+',' ALPHA ').replace('(?!(BD-))','')
            s = s.replace('^','').replace('$','').replace('(','').replace(')','').replace('?','').replace('*','').replace('+','')
            s = re.sub(r'\s+',' ',s).strip()
            if 1 <= len(s) <= 70: out.add(s)
    return out

descs = sorted(corpus_from('/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/IDBI.py') |
               corpus_from('/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Indusind.py') |
               {'RAM KUMAR','', 'SOME MERCHANT PVT LTD','ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES','GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR',
                'ACH-BD-ACME INDUSTRIES','ACH-ACME','NACH/ABC/1','E MANDATE CHARGES','POS TXN-MERCHANT MID0123'})
remarks = ['', '123', '1234', '12345', '123456', '1234567', '0000000000012345', 'Cheque Drawn(Paid)', 'ABC123']
amounts = [1, 2, -1, -2, 5, 9, 10, 99, 100, 7000, 55000]
types   = ['DEBIT','CREDIT']
accts   = ['SAVING','CURRENT','OVER_DRAFT']

pairs = [('IDBI', '/tmp/opencode/orig/IDBI_orig.py', '/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/IDBI.py'),
         ('Indusind','/tmp/opencode/orig/Indusind_orig.py','/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Indusind.py')]

cols=['transactionCategory','transactionSubcategory','partyName']
for bank, po, pn in pairs:
    fo = load(po, bank+'_o'); fn = load(pn, bank+'_n')
    total=0; diffs=[]
    for at in accts:
        rows=[{'description':d,'remark':r,'type':t,'amount':a}
              for d in descs for r in remarks for t in types for a in amounts]
        # run one row at a time in chunks but keep rows isolated from shift() effects by using unique amounts? keep as is
        A = run(fo, [dict(x) for x in rows], accountType=at).reset_index(drop=True)
        B = run(fn, [dict(x) for x in rows], accountType=at).reset_index(drop=True)
        total += len(rows)
        neq = (A[cols].astype(str) != B[cols].astype(str)).any(axis=1)
        for idx in A.index[neq]:
            diffs.append((at, rows[idx], tuple(A.loc[idx,cols]), tuple(B.loc[idx,cols])))
    print(f"===== {bank}: {total} rows compared, {len(diffs)} differing")
    # summarise diff classes
    from collections import Counter
    c = Counter((at, a, b) for at,_,a,b in diffs)
    for (at,a,b),n in c.most_common():
        print(f"  [{at}] x{n}:  {a}  ->  {b}")
    for at,r,a,b in diffs[:6]:
        print("   e.g.", at, r, a, "->", b)

import sys, re, importlib.util
import pandas as pd
sys.path.insert(0,'/app/categorizationapp')
from harness import run

def load(path, name):
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
    m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m)
    return [v for k,v in vars(m).items() if k.startswith('categorize_')][0]

def corpus_from(path):
    src=open(path).read(); out=set()
    for lit in re.findall(r'(?:description|partyName|party2)\.str\.contains\(\s*"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"', src):
        for alt in lit.split('|'):
            s=alt.replace('\\\\b','').replace('\\b','').replace('\\s?',' ').replace('\\s*','').replace('\\.','.')
            s=re.sub(r'\[([A-Za-z])[A-Za-z]*\]', r'\1', s)
            s=re.sub(r'\[0-9\]\{(\d+)(,\d*)?\}', lambda m:'1'*int(m.group(1)), s)
            s=re.sub(r'\[A-Z\]\{(\d+)(,\d*)?\}', lambda m:'A'*int(m.group(1)), s)
            s=s.replace('[0-9]','7').replace('[A-Z]','K').replace('[A-z]','K')
            s=re.sub(r'\{\d+(,\d*)?\}','',s)
            s=s.replace('.*',' ALPHA BETA ').replace('.+',' ALPHA ').replace('(?!(BD-))','')
            s=re.sub(r'[\^\$\(\)\?\*\+]','',s); s=re.sub(r'\s+',' ',s).strip()
            if 1<=len(s)<=70: out.add(s)
    return out

IDBI_O='/tmp/opencode/orig/IDBI_orig.py'; IDBI_N='/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/IDBI.py'
IND_O='/tmp/opencode/orig/Indusind_orig.py'; IND_N='/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Indusind.py'
descs = sorted(corpus_from(IDBI_N) | corpus_from(IND_N) | {
 'RAM KUMAR','','SOME MERCHANT PVT LTD','ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES','GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR',
 'ACH-BD-ACME INDUSTRIES','ACH-ACME','NACH/ABC/1','POS TXN-MERCHANT MID0123','ETPC ACH-BD-XYZ LTD',
 'HDFCH0123456789 SITA DEVI','UPI/123/456/RAM','IMPS/123/456/RAM','NEFT/CMS/1/ABC','CHEQUE DEPOSIT'})
remarks=['','123','1234','12345','123456','1234567','0000000000012345','Cheque Drawn(Paid)','ABC123','12345678901234']
amounts=[1,2,-1,-2,5,9,10,99,7000]
types=['DEBIT','CREDIT']; accts=['SAVING','CURRENT','OVER_DRAFT','CREDIT_CARD']
cols=['transactionCategory','transactionSubcategory','partyName']

def classes(bank, row, a, b):
    d=row['description']; r=row['remark']; t=row['type']; amt=row['amount']
    if bank=='IDBI':
        if re.match(r'^ACH-BD-NACH', d, re.I) and a[0]==b[0] and a[1]==b[1]: return 'A: IDBI ACH-BD-NACH payee'
        if re.match(r'^[A-Z]{5}[0-9]{10,}', d) and a[0]==b[0] and a[1]==b[1]: return 'B: IDBI IFSC-like ref payee'
    else:
        if re.fullmatch(r'[0-9]{6}', r or '') and t=='DEBIT' and b[0]=='CHEQUE_PAID': return 'C: Indusind 6-digit cheque remark'
        if re.search(r'mandate', d, re.I) and amt in (1,2,-1,-2) and b[0]=='ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION': return 'D: Indusind mandate token'
        if re.search(r'\bPOS TXN', d, re.I) and t=='CREDIT' and amt>=10 and b[0]=='CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL': return 'E: Indusind card reversal (SAVING)'
    return 'UNEXPECTED'

from collections import Counter
for bank,po,pn in [('IDBI',IDBI_O,IDBI_N),('Indusind',IND_O,IND_N)]:
    fo=load(po,bank+'_o'); fn=load(pn,bank+'_n')
    tally=Counter(); unexpected=[]; total=0
    for at in accts:
        rows=[{'description':d,'remark':'','type':t,'amount':a} for d in descs for t in types for a in amounts]
        rows+=[{'description':d,'remark':r,'type':t,'amount':7000} for d in descs for r in remarks for t in types]
        rows+=[{'description':d,'remark':r,'type':t,'amount':a} for d in ['RAM KUMAR','POS TXN-MERCHANT MID0123','E MANDATE CHARGES','TRF TO RAM/123456','GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR','ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES'] for r in remarks for t in types for a in amounts]
        A=run(fo,[dict(x) for x in rows],accountType=at).reset_index(drop=True)
        B=run(fn,[dict(x) for x in rows],accountType=at).reset_index(drop=True)
        total+=len(rows)
        neq=(A[cols].astype(str)!=B[cols].astype(str)).any(axis=1)
        for idx in A.index[neq]:
            k=classes(bank,rows[idx],tuple(A.loc[idx,cols]),tuple(B.loc[idx,cols]))
            tally[(at,k)]+=1
            if k=='UNEXPECTED' and len(unexpected)<25:
                unexpected.append((at,rows[idx],tuple(A.loc[idx,cols]),tuple(B.loc[idx,cols])))
    print(f"===== {bank}: {total} rows compared")
    for (at,k),n in sorted(tally.items()): print(f"   {at:12s} {k:38s} {n}")
    print("   UNEXPECTED samples:", len(unexpected))
    for u in unexpected: print("     ", u)

steps.message:
## Root cause

The blast radius was narrower than the ticket suggested. Comparing file timestamps against the upstream snapshot showed that of the 54 files in the service, exactly two had been modified after import:

```
2022-11-02 10:23:12   (all 52 other files)
2026-07-15 02:30:30   BankScripts/IDBI.py
2026-07-15 02:30:30   BankScripts/Indusind.py
```

All five reported forms trace to five single-token defects in those two rule tables — everything else in the labeling path is untouched upstream code.

## The five defects and fixes

| Ticket | Location | Defect | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| Salary shows `NACH` instead of employer | `IDBI.py:83` | `^ACH-BD-NACH` took dash-token **2**, which *is* the literal `NACH` the pattern matched — the rule was also a dead duplicate of line 84 | take token **3** (the payee) |
| Inbound transfer name blank | `IDBI.py:110` | `py_extract(pat="[0-9]{10,} (.*)", index=1)` on a **one**-group regex → `.get(1)` is `None`, so it always returned `""` (only out-of-range `py_extract` in the repo) | `index=0` |
| Cheque filed as general transfer | `Indusind.py:64` | remark rule was `^[0-9]{5}$` — the only single-fixed-width cheque rule in the codebase; every sibling bank uses a range, and the file's own payee rule at line 190 keys on `[0-9]{5,}`, so 6-digit cheque numbers fell through to `TRANSFER` | `^[0-9]{5,6}$` (matches Axis/BOM/PNB convention) |
| Mandate token filed as transfer | `Indusind.py:30` | `amount.eq(2)` only, so the ₹1 nominal token missed the verification rule | `amount.isin([1,2,-1,-2])`, mirroring the file's own `isin([1,-1])` nominal-amount idiom |
| Card refund labelled `REFUND` not `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL` | `Indusind.py:26` | `accountType=="SAVINGS"` — the canonical value is `"SAVING"` everywhere (including the very next line and line 95), so the rule could never fire and savings rows fell through to the `REFUND` rule | `accountType=="SAVING"` |

## Verification

- All five customer narrations now label and name correctly (`ACME INDUSTRIES`, `RAVI KUMAR`, `CHEQUE_PAID`, `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`, `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL` on savings / `CARD_RECEIPTS` on current).
- Differential run of old vs new code over **85,640 rows per bank** (corpus generated from every regex literal in both files, crossed with remark widths, nominal/normal amounts, both directions, and all four account types): every single difference falls into one of the five intended classes, **0 unexpected changes**. The account-type-dependent change appears only under `SAVING`, as intended.
- Neighbouring forms confirmed untouched: `ACH-BD-`/`ACH-BARB-`/`ACH-` payees, 5-digit and 7-digit remarks, `MNDTVRFCHGS` charges, ₹4500 mandate EMI debits, sub-₹10 POS refunds, and ordinary UPI/POS/NEFT rows.

One thing to flag separately (**not** introduced here, and left alone): `SalaryDetection.py:212` drops its temporary `dateSal` period column only inside the `salaryDetect == True` branch. When no salary is detected on a `SAVING` account the column survives into `to_json`, and under the *installed* pandas 2.2.3 that raises `OverflowError` → HTTP 500. It reproduces identically on the pre-fix code with unrelated rows, and the pinned `pandas==1.2.4` serializes Period columns fine, so it's an environment-drift landmine rather than part of this incident — worth its own ticket.
